title: House View
summary: Current working theses across AI infrastructure, agent workflows, valuation discipline, and macro risk. This is the map before the archive.

theses.title: AI physical bottlenecks are becoming the investable edge
theses.claim: The AI trade is shifting from model excitement toward power, packaging, memory, cooling, and interconnect scarcity.
theses.whatChanged: Power, advanced packaging, and memory evidence strengthened; optics and brownfield liquid cooling remain threshold-gated rather than fully proven.
theses.wouldChangeView: Evidence that hyperscalers can source power, memory, and advanced packaging faster than current lead-time signals imply.

theses.title: The AI theme is real; expression risk is now the hard part
theses.claim: The current AI run is healthier than prior theme bubbles at the leader level, but second-order names increasingly price future demand before economics are proven.
theses.whatChanged: The AI-versus-climate-cycle comparison showed the analogy is useful for valuation discipline, not for declaring AI a fake bubble.
theses.wouldChangeView: A broad earnings inflection across second-order beneficiaries that makes high multiples fall without a price reset.

theses.title: Agent workflows need control systems, not more prompt theater
theses.claim: Production agent quality comes from hooks, evals, checkpoints, handoffs, and operational discipline more than from one clever prompt.
theses.whatChanged: The site now has multiple AI-operator pieces converging on workflow architecture as the real bottleneck.
theses.wouldChangeView: Evidence that frontier-model capability alone removes the need for explicit workflow gates in production use.

theses.title: China AI exposure splits into platform quality and infrastructure leverage
theses.claim: The better China AI opportunities are not always the flashiest models; cloud, platforms, power equipment, and operating leverage matter more.
theses.whatChanged: Recent watchlist work separated valuation-sane platform exposure from crowded AI-infra trades.
theses.wouldChangeView: Regulatory, geopolitical, or margin evidence that overwhelms the AI/platform monetization path.

clusters.title: AI Physical Bottlenecks
clusters.summary: Power, cooling, memory, packaging, and infrastructure constraints behind the AI buildout.
clusters.thesis: The market is increasingly pricing AI as a physical infrastructure problem, not only a model/software problem.
clusters.wouldChangeView: Clear evidence that bottleneck lead times normalize without margin pressure, capex overshoot, or delayed data-center delivery.

clusters.title: AI Valuation Discipline
clusters.summary: Theme-cycle comparisons, expensive narrative checks, and risk/reward discipline for AI equities.
clusters.thesis: AI is not automatically a bubble, but the market can still overpay for weak expressions of a real theme.
clusters.wouldChangeView: Broad earnings and FCF conversion across second-order AI names that validates the multiples without a drawdown.

clusters.title: Agent Workflow Discipline
clusters.summary: Hooks, handoffs, slides-as-software, coding agents, and operational control layers for real agent work.
clusters.thesis: Useful agents are not just model calls; they are controlled systems with explicit gates, reusable skills, eval loops, and workflow memory.
clusters.wouldChangeView: A reliable pattern where model capability alone replaces structured workflow control in production environments.

clusters.title: China AI Platforms and Infrastructure
clusters.summary: China AI platform exposure, infrastructure picks-and-shovels, and valuation-sane ways to express the theme.
clusters.thesis: China AI exposure should be split between platform monetization quality and infrastructure leverage rather than treated as one broad beta trade.
clusters.wouldChangeView: Evidence that policy/geopolitical risk or platform margin pressure dominates AI monetization and infrastructure demand.
